I used the **Thompson–Cox–Hastings (TCH) pseudo-Voigt**, Edi’s `cwl-tch-pseudo-voigt`, without the FCJ axial-divergence correction.

For displacement \(x=2\theta-2\theta_{\text{peak}}\), the normalized peak shape is

\[
p(x)=(1-\eta)\,G(x;H)+\eta\,L(x;H),
\]

where both components have the same FWHM \(H\):

\[
G(x;H)=\frac{2\sqrt{\ln2}}{H\sqrt{\pi}}
\exp\!\left[-4\ln2\left(\frac{x}{H}\right)^2\right],
\]

\[
L(x;H)=\frac{2}{\pi H}
\frac{1}{1+4(x/H)^2}.
\]

The Gaussian and Lorentzian component widths depend on the **Bragg angle** \(\theta\):

\[
H_G^2=U\tan^2\theta+V\tan\theta+W,
\qquad
H_L=X\tan\theta+\frac{Y}{\cos\theta}.
\]

TCH combines these widths through

\[
\begin{aligned}
H^5={}&H_G^5+2.69269H_G^4H_L
+2.42843H_G^3H_L^2\\
&+4.47163H_G^2H_L^3
+0.07842H_GH_L^4+H_L^5,
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\eta=1.36603r-0.47719r^2+0.11116r^3,
\qquad r=\frac{H_L}{H}.
\]

Thus, \(\eta\) is calculated from the widths rather than refined independently. These are the [standard TCH equations](https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1222688).

Your saved coefficients are:

| Coefficient | Value ± uncertainty |
|---|---:|
| \(U\) | \(0.0837 \pm 0.0035\) °² |
| \(V\) | \(-0.1365 \pm 0.0074\) °² |
| \(W\) | \(0.1454 \pm 0.0048\) °² |
| \(X\) | \(0.067 \pm 0.015\) ° |
| \(Y\) | \(0.0254 \pm 0.0095\) ° |

The widths \(H_G,H_L,H\) are expressed in degrees of \(2\theta\).
